issues.legal_issue: Pension and retirement benefits arising from an employee’s service are payable according to the applicable service rules, and a person who married the employee while his existing marriage subsisted cannot claim recognition as his legally wedded wife for that entitlement.
material_facts: The deceased employee’s first marriage was still subsisting when he entered a subsequent marriage.
After the employee’s death, competing claimants disputed entitlement to pension and other retirement benefits arising from his service.
The High Court directed that those benefits be given to the woman from the subsequent marriage and her daughter.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s direction concerning pensionary benefits was set aside. The benefits were to be given by the employer to the appellants in accordance with the service rules governing the deceased employee.
issues.legal_principle: Pension is normally given to the legally wedded wife of a deceased employee. A woman who married the employee while his prior marriage was subsisting could not be treated as his legally wedded wife for this purpose; entitlement to pensionary benefits is governed by the applicable service rules. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.service_benefit_entitlement_dispute: Claimants disputed who was entitled to pension or other retirement benefits arising from a deceased person’s employment.
predicates.prior_marriage_subsisted_at_later_marria: The employee entered a later marriage while an earlier marriage remained subsisting.
predicates.deceased_was_an_employee: The deceased person had been employed and the disputed benefits arose from that employment.

issues.definition: When a deceased employee’s service benefits are disputed and a later marriage occurred while an earlier marriage subsisted, the benefits are paid to claimants eligible under the applicable service rules.

issues.legal_issue: Structures forming part of a house described in a will pass to the will’s beneficiaries when the will bequeaths that house and the deceased’s immovable properties.
material_facts: The will described a house and bequeathed it to the beneficiaries.
The disputed shops had been constructed within the premises and formed part of that house.
The trial court treated the shops as covered by the bequest, and the Supreme Court rejected the challenge to that conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The shops formed part of the house bequeathed by the will and were to pass to the will’s beneficiaries; the appellants’ claim to inherit them was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the description and scope of the bequest: where a will describes and bequeaths a house, structures forming part of that house are included, particularly where the will bequeaths the deceased’s immovable properties. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.will_and_property_succession_dispute: A succession dispute concerned whether property passed under a will.
predicates.will_bequeaths_described_house: The will described a house and bequeathed it to designated beneficiaries.
predicates.disputed_structures_form_part_of_house: The disputed structures were located within the premises and formed part of the described house.

issues.definition: When a succession dispute concerns structures forming part of a house bequeathed by a will, those structures pass to the will’s beneficiaries.
